correctness.rationale: Bias correction makes the exact first LAMB direction \(r_i=(Hx)_i/(|(Hx)_i|+\varepsilon)\). A self-contained spectral-moment argument proves \(\cos\angle(x,Hx)\ge2\sqrt{\kappa}/(\kappa+1)\). A coordinate-quadrant lemma proves that \(x^\top r\le0\) would force \(\angle(x,Hx)>\pi/4\). The threshold \(\kappa=3+2\sqrt2\) follows exactly, and a rotated endpoint-spectrum family proves sharpness for every fixed positive \(\varepsilon\).

value.rationale: LAMB's defining mechanism combines coordinatewise Adam preconditioning with layerwise norm control, and later work explicitly targets instability of its trust ratio. The theorem isolates a different, irreducibly directional failure mode with an exact condition-number threshold: beyond \(3+2\sqrt2\), positive scalar control of the layer step cannot prevent first-step distance growth on some SPD problems. This gives a concrete boundary between magnitude stabilization and directional stabilization.
